Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  May 7, 2026

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on May 7, 2026. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Ashley Ferrette announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Christopher
  Beck - District 4, Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at
  Large
  Absent:  District 2 - Vacant, District 3 - Vacant

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Kaderick Burns  Recreation Supervisor
  Baz Devlia  Human Services Superintendent
  Craig Civitello  Park Maintenance Supervisor
  Ashley Ferrette  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and second by Commissioner Beck that
the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on February 5, 2026
and March 5, 2026, be approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioner Denmon, Commissioner Brown and Commissioner Beck
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Park Maintenance Supervisor Craig Civitello reported
the following: Parks Division - Staff is upgrading the burglar alarm and fire protection
systems at the Centinela Adobe. This month, Mariposa Landscapes will begin maintenance
of the City’s medians and parkways. As a result, City staff will shift their primary focus to
park maintenance. Graffiti Division - Last month, staff met with the Inglewood Police
Department to discuss graffiti at City parks, particularly at Edward Vincent Park. Since that
meeting, police presence at Edward Vincent Park has increased and incidents of graffiti
have decreased. Staff are transitioning from manual paper tracking to iPads to better
document graffiti removal activities and improve reporting. Unfortunately, the transition

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

from paper to paperless tracking has presented some technical challenges. As a result, staff
does not yet have complete graffiti removal data for the month of February. Tree Division
- City crews have wrapped up trimming at Rogers Park and Siminski Park. They will be
heading over to Darby Park next week. City contractor crews have started the annual ficus
and chinese elm pruning and should be done by July.

REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor Kaderick Burns reported the following:
Memorial Day - Join the City of Inglewood for the 77th Annual Memorial Day Service on
Monday, May 25, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. The event will be held at Inglewood City Hall, in front
of the Memorial monument on the south lawn. This solemn ceremony honors the brave
men and women of the United States Armed Forces who made the ultimate sacrifice in
service to our nation. Let us come together to reflect, remember, and express our deepest
gratitude to those who gave their lives in defense of our freedoms. Summer Day Camp -
Our 2026 Full Day Summer Day Camp will begin June 15th to August 7th with a total of four
sessions. Each session runs two consecutive weeks filled with games, creative activities,
sports, enrichment experiences, field trips, and more. Day Camp hours are from 9:00 a.m.
to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. We also provide before and after care between 7:00
a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. Pilates -The Parks, Recreation and Community
Services Department invites you to grab your pilate socks and meet us on the mat for
Pilates in the Wood! Join us for a low-impact, highly effective mat Pilates class that
strengthens and lengthens the body from the inside out. Participants will enjoy a full-body
workout that builds core strength, flexibility, posture, balance, and mobility in a
welcoming, energizing environment. The benefits of Mat Pilates include; building strength
and endurance, improving muscle tone and posture, reducing stress and tension, and
increasing flexibility and mobility. Classes are held on Mondays and Wednesdays from 6:00
p.m. to 7:00 p.m. at Rogers Park, and on Saturdays from 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. at the
Veterans Memorial Building. The cost is $20 per class, and the classes are open to students
18 and older. For more information on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city
sports website at https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Superintendent Baz Devlia reported on the
following: Senior Center Activities - May is another exciting month for our Senior Center.
Today, our third Tennis Class Workshops started at Vincent Park from 9:00 a.m. – 10:00
a.m. On May 8, we will have a special Mother’s Day Program from 10:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m.
with a special performance by the Inspirational Choir, poetry, and a raffle for a “Spa Day”
trip. May 11 will be an incredibly exciting day, the Mayoral Initiative Blue Zone Project will
be presented to our seniors from 11:00 a.m. – 11:45 a.m. The aforementioned spa day
takes place on May 13, when will be taking our seniors to El Camino College for a special
pampering which includes hair, nails, and facials from 9:00 a.m. – 12:00noon. On May 14,
we will be showing the movie “Collateral Beauty”. On May 15, the Inglewood Police
Department will conduct a presentation on “fraud” from 10:30 a.m. – 11:00 a.m. On May

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

18, LA County of Mental Health will be conducting a presentation on “Managing Your
Medication” from 10:45 a.m. – 11:45 a.m. On May 28, we will have a spectacular dance.
Elderly Nutrition Program - We proudly serve approximately 460 seniors each day through
both home-delivered meals for homebound individuals and congregate dining services. To
further support our community's nutritional needs, monthly shelf-stable meal boxes are
provided in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank. Our Nutrition Program has
recently completed distributing Emergency Meals. Emergency Meals are ready-to-eat food
items designed to be kept on hand in the event of an emergency. This summer, we are
getting ready for the distribution of Farmers' Market cards, and seniors have already
enjoyed trips to local markets through our transportation services. Senior Center
Paratransit - Our paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors and the
disabled community in Inglewood and Hawthorne. Every so often, bus operators
participate in online driver training. This time around, the topic is distracted driving. All bus
operators completed a refresher training on distracted driving as well as an in class session
with the fleet department on how to properly pre-trip their vehicles. On Saturday, May 2,
2026, the Trolley Bus participated in the city’s second annual Touch-A-Truck event that
was held at Rogers Park. The kids enjoyed viewing all the large vehicles that participated
at this year’s event.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department Director
Thomas Uwal reported on the following: World Cup Community Events - The City of
Inglewood, through a grant from the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
Authority (Metro), will host two community events on Market Street in celebration of the
2026 FIFA World Cup. These events are scheduled for June 12, 2026, and July 10, 2026 and
will bring the community together through food, entertainment, and cultural activities.
SoFi Stadium in Inglewood will serve as a major host venue for the 2026 FIFA World Cup,
featuring eight matches, including the opening game for the U.S. Men’s National Team.
The tournament will run from June 11 through July 19, 2026, and the stadium will host five
group stage matches, two Round of 32 matches, and one quarterfinal match. 5th Annual
Women Rock Empowerment Summit - The 5th Annual Women Rock Empowerment
Summit will be held on May 2, 2026, from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the Inglewood Senior
Center. The summit will feature workshops, guest speakers, and networking opportunities
designed to support the professional and personal growth of women in our community.
This free community event is hosted annually by Councilwoman Dionne Faulk and City
Clerk Aisha Thompson. We encourage our Commissioners to attend and support this
important event. Jason Crowe, Jr. Commendation - The Inglewood City Council, along with
the Parks, Recreation and Community Services Commissioners, proudly recognized Jason
Crowe, Jr., a standout basketball player from Inglewood High School, for making history as
California’s all-time leading high school basketball scorer with an extraordinary 4,718
career points. Jason’s remarkable achievement reflects years of dedication, discipline, and
passion for the game of basketball. He is truly a product of the Inglewood Parks, Recreation

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

and Community Services Department. From a young age, he developed his skills on the
basketball courts in our city parks, where his talent and determination first began to shine.
Through hard work and perseverance, Jason has grown into one of the most prolific scorers
in high school basketball history. Continuing his impressive journey, Jason Crowe, Jr. has
officially signed with the University of Missouri Men’s Basketball Team, taking the next
step toward what promises to be an outstanding collegiate and athletic career. We thank
our Commissioners for recognizing and celebrating his remarkable accomplishments. Park
and Recreation Commissioners Update - Effective Tuesday, March 17, Commissioner
Octavio Padilla will transition from the Park and Recreation Commission to serve on the
Building Permit Commission. Today marks his final day serving as a Park and Recreation
Commissioner. We sincerely thank Commissioner Padilla for his dedication and
contributions to our Department and wish him continued success in his new role.
Councilman Alex Padilla will be appointing a new Park and Recreation Commissioner in the
near future. Additionally, we are currently awaiting appointment from Councilman
Morales to fill the current vacancy.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Brown asked staff to email him the event
flyer for the 2026 events and activities to share the information in his community.
Commissioner Beck thanked all who played a part in the youth basketball tournament
hosted at the Intuit Dome for the Parks Boys and Girls basketball team championship.
Commissioner Denmon asked for a moment of silence for Cache Beck, Luis Canche, and
Wendy Hamilton.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:49 p.m.
